title: getfield
summary: Access struct or object fields in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: Direct field retrieval is metadata-only and preserves resident handles. The independently gated indexed-resident form gathers authoritative storage through the owning provider.

description: `value = getfield(S, field)` returns the contents of `S.field`. Nested field access and structure-array indexing follow MATLAB semantics; RunMat object-family access is a separately gated extension.
behaviors: Field names must be character vectors or string scalars. Several field names in a row navigate nested structs: `getfield(S, "outer", "inner")` is equivalent to `S.outer.inner`.
When `S` is a struct array, `getfield(S, "field")` examines the first element by default. Provide indices in a cell array to target another element: `getfield(S, {k}, "field")` yields `S(k).field`.

After a field name you may supply an index cell to subscript the field value, e.g. `getfield(S, "values", {row, col})`. Numeric indices accept exact positive scalar or vector values from every integer class, and logical vectors select matching elements.
Direct integer field access and host subarray selection preserve the field's exact class, shape, storage, and magnitude; an index class never determines the output class.

RunMat mode additionally accepts textual `end` or numeric selectors, object/handle/listener/exception property access, and indexed resident-field gather. Each family is independently disabled in MATLAB-compatible modes.
Directly retrieved resident fields retain their original handle without provider access. Indexed resident fields use the explicit RunMat-only typed host-gather form and return host data.

faqs.question: Does `getfield` work on non-struct values?
faqs.answer: The MATLAB-compatible surface requires a scalar or nonscalar structure. RunMat mode additionally supports selected object, handle, listener, and exception values through an explicit extension gate.

faqs.question: How do I access nested struct fields?
faqs.answer: Provide every level explicitly: `getfield(S, "parent", "child", "leaf")` traverses the same path as `S.parent.child.leaf`.

faqs.question: How do I read from a struct array?
faqs.answer: Supply a cell array of indices before the first field name. For example, `getfield(S, {3}, "value")` mirrors `S(3).value`. Indices are one-based like MATLAB.

faqs.question: Can I index the value stored in a field?
faqs.answer: Yes. Supply numeric or logical values inside an index cell. RunMat mode also provides a separately gated textual `end` convenience.

faqs.question: Do dependent properties run their getter methods?
faqs.answer: In RunMat mode, yes. Object-family access is a RunMat extension; dependent properties invoke `get.<name>` when available, otherwise the backing field `<property>_backing` is inspected.

faqs.question: What happens when I query a deleted handle object?
faqs.answer: The RunMat object-family extension raises `Invalid or deleted handle object 'ClassName'.`

gpu_residency: Direct field access is metadata-only and preserves an existing resident handle. Indexing into a resident field is a separately gated RunMat form that gathers exact typed storage to the host.
gpu_behavior: Direct resident field retrieval performs no provider operation. Indexed resident-field access is not presented as metadata-only: in RunMat mode it routes through the owning provider, downloads authoritative storage, and returns a host result; MATLAB-compatible modes reject it before provider access.
